entities.summary: Martín del Barco Centenera was a Spanish cleric, explorer, and author who played a significant role in the early modern period of European history. Born in 1535 in Logrosán, Spain, Centenera was educated at the University of Salamanca and later became a priest. He was part of the Spanish Inquisition and participated in the suppression of the Moriscos, a Muslim minority living in Spain. Centenera also traveled to the Americas and wrote about his experiences in his book 'Tratado de la conquista del Nuevo Mundo'. He died in 1602 and left behind a legacy as a prominent figure in the history of Spanish exploration and colonization. His writings provide valuable insights into the cultural and religious tensions of the time. Centenera's story is a testament to the complex and often fraught history of the Spanish Empire. His work continues to be studied by historians today.
